exposure: duration of the active phase of the first stage of labor
z score of the head-to-perineum distance
cohort: 951 women with singleton pregnancies who underwent midcavity vacuum-assisted delivery
finding: Maternal height, duration of active labor, non-occiput anterior fetal head position, head-to-perineum distance, and birthweight >4000g were independently associated with failed midcavity vacuum-assisted delivery.
mod_finding: A high fetal head station, measured using the head-to-perineum distance, and a non-occiput anterior position of the fetal head were independently associated with failed midcavity vacuum-assisted delivery.
